predecessors.name: Principality of Hungary
predecessors.text: Prince Geza's Hungary, which Stephen I turned into a kingdom by his coronation at Esztergom on 25 December 1000

successors.name: Habsburg monarchy
successors.text: royal Hungary: 'The territory of present-day Slovakia and northwestern Transdanubia were parts of this polity' (Royal Hungary page); Cliopatria draws these cells in its Kingdom of Spain row from 1540

successors.name: Ottoman Empire
successors.text: central Hungary taken with Buda on 29 August 1541 and made Budin Province (Ottoman Hungary infobox area about 91,250 km2)

successors.name: Eastern Hungarian Kingdom
successors.text: Transylvania and the eastern plain held by John Zapolya, 'after 1571 known as Partium'

ledger.x: 1000: Stephen I is crowned first king of Hungary at Esztergom on Christmas Day.
c.1002-1003: Stephen I invades Transylvania and seizes his uncle Gyula.
c.1003: Slovakia passes to Poland under Boleslaw I.
1010: Cliopatria adds a strip of the Iron Gates and Banat edge on the Danube from the First Bulgarian Empire.
c.1014: the Polish-Hungarian war over Slovakia begins.
1015: Cliopatria withdraws the south-eastern Danube strip it added in 1010.
January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen returns Slovakia to Hungary.
January 1018: the Peace of Bautzen ends the Polish-Hungarian war.
1031: Conrad II cedes the land between the Lajta and the Fischa to Hungary.
1040: Cliopatria adds 33 cells on the south-eastern edge (Banat and Oltenia edge).
1091: Ladislaus I crosses the Drava and conquers Slavonia.
1091: Hungary begins the struggle for Croatia proper beyond Gvozd.
1102: Coloman is crowned king of Croatia and Dalmatia at Biograd.
1102: the Biograd coronation ends the Croatian succession struggle.
1105: Zadar, Split and the other Dalmatian towns accept Coloman's suzerainty.
1116: Venice seizes Biograd, Split, Trogir, Sibenik, Zadar and the islands after Coloman's death.
1133: Bela II wins back the Dalmatian cities except Zadar.
1139: Cliopatria adds 11 cells on the north-western edge (the Polish and Moravian border) to the kingdom.
Summer 1164: a Byzantine army occupies Syrmia, which becomes a Byzantine theme.
Spring 1165: the Byzantines occupy Dalmatia.
8 July 1167: the Byzantines destroy the Hungarian army at Sirmium and take central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia by treaty.
Early 1181: after Manuel I's death Bela III restores Hungarian suzerainty over Dalmatia, and Zadar accepts it.
By May 1182: Bela III holds Syrmia again.
1188: Bela III invades Halych, expels Roman Mstislavich and gives the principality to his son Andrew.
1189-1190: Vladimir escapes and, with Casimir II of Poland, expels Andrew from Halych.
1202: the Fourth Crusade takes Zadar from the Hungarian crown.
1202: Cliopatria adds the Belgrade-Branicevo country to Hungary.
1206: Cliopatria returns the Belgrade-Branicevo country to Bulgaria.
1216: Cliopatria again adds the Belgrade-Branicevo country.
1227: the Cuman chieftain Boricius acknowledges Bela's suzerainty; Bela takes the title King of Cumania in 1233.
1231: Bela founds the march of Szoreny (the Banate of Severin) in Oltenia.
1235: Duke Coloman and Bishop John open the five-year Bosnian Crusade.
1236: Cliopatria returns the Belgrade-Branicevo country to Bulgaria.
1241: Coloman withdraws from Bosnia after the Tatar invasion and Ninoslav retakes it.
1241: the Mongol conquest ends Bela's suzerainty east of the Carpathians.
11 April 1241: the Mongols annihilate Bela IV's army at Mohi and occupy Hungary east of the Danube.
March 1242: Batu withdraws the Mongol army from Hungary after Ogodei's death.
1250s: Bela IV pacifies Bosnia and controls northern Usora and Soli through vassal rulers.
1 May 1254: by the Peace of Pressburg Ottokar II cedes Styria to Bela IV.
1255: Rostislav, Ban of Macso, forces Tsar Michael Asen I to cede Belgrade and Branicevo.
31 March 1261: by the Peace of Vienna Bela IV renounces Styria in favour of Ottokar II.
1294: Cliopatria hands 64 north-eastern cells (Carpathian Ruthenia) to Galicia-Volhynia.
14 January 1301: Andrew III dies and the Arpad dynasty ends; the crown passes to the Angevins after the 1301-1308 interregnum.
1305: Slovakia slips from royal control into the domain of Matthew Csak.
c.1305: Paul Subic and the Babonic family make themselves independent in Croatia and Slavonia.
ledger.cp: Paul Subic and the Babonic family

ledger.x: 1305: Cliopatria returns 52 north-eastern cells (Carpathian Ruthenia) to Hungary from Galicia-Volhynia.
1321: Matthew Csak dies and his Slovak domain returns to the crown.
1323: Charles I subjugates the Babonic and Subic families and recovers Croatia and Slavonia.
ledger.cp: Paul Subic and the Babonic family

ledger.x: 1324: Stephen II Kotromanic annexes Usora and Soli from the Hungarian crown.
1333: Cliopatria hands 26 south-western cells (Dalmatian hinterland) to the Banate of Bosnia.
24 December 1347: Louis I enters the Kingdom of Naples near L'Aquila.
1351: Louis I withdraws all his troops from the Kingdom of Naples.
18 February 1358: by the Treaty of Zadar Venice gives up all Dalmatia between the Gulf of Kvarner and Durazzo to Louis I.
18 February 1358: the Treaty of Zadar ends the contest for Zadar.
Spring 1363: Louis I invades Bosnia from two directions.
1363: Cliopatria adds 21 eastern cells (the Moldavian march) taken from the Golden Horde.
May-June 1365: Louis I seizes Vidin and imprisons Tsar Ivan Stratsimir; his troops occupy the realm within three months.
March 1367: Tvrtko I returns and regains Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum and Usora.
March 1367: Tvrtko I recovers the Bosnian lands Louis had taken.
c.1369: Hungarian control of Vidin ends.
1387: Sigismund of Luxembourg becomes king, co-ruling from 1387 and alone from 1395.
1409: Ladislaus of Naples sells his rights in Dalmatia to Venice.
1415: Venice holds the Dalmatian coast, which Cliopatria removes from the Hungarian shape.
c.1415: the contest for the Dalmatian coast ends in Venetian hands.
Late 1437: Sigismund dies and the Estates elect Albert of Habsburg king.
24 January 1458: the Estates proclaim Matthias Hunyadi king.
After 19 July 1463: Matthias conquers Jajce and northern Bosnia, organised as the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik.
31 March 1468: Matthias declares war on George of Podebrady and invades Moravia and Silesia.
15 August 1475: the Prince of Moldavia swears fealty to Matthias.
15 February 1476: Matthias captures Sabac on the Sava from the Ottomans.
1477: Matthias invades Lower Austria and blockades Vienna.
1 December 1477: peace with Frederick III, who promises to confirm Matthias as ruler of Bohemia.
21 July 1478: the Peace of Olomouc leaves Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia to Matthias and Bohemia proper to Vladislaus Jagiellon.
21 July 1478: the Peace of Olomouc ends the Bohemian war.
1482: Matthias begins to occupy Lower Austria; the Black Army takes Vienna in 1485.
1485: Matthias moves his court to Vienna.
1487: Matthias takes Wiener Neustadt and the title Duke of Austria, and holds Styria.
1490: after Matthias's death on 6 April, Frederick III regains the Austrian lands without a serious fight.
1490: Styria returns to the Habsburgs with the rest of Matthias's Austrian conquests.
1490: the court returns from Vienna to Buda.
1490: Matthias dies and Moldavia's fealty lapses.
1490: Matthias dies and Vladislaus II of Bohemia succeeds as king of Hungary.
1491: the Peace of Pressburg returns Matthias's conquests: Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia go back to Bohemia, Austria to the Habsburgs.
1521: Suleiman seizes Belgrade.
29 August 1526: Louis II is killed at Mohacs and the crown passes to rival kings.
1526: Cliopatria drops 34 southern cells (Syrmia and southern Baranya) after Mohacs.
1 January 1527: the Croatian parliament at Cetin elects Ferdinand of Habsburg king of Croatia.
By 1528: Ferdinand's army drives John Zapolya out of the country; the two kings contest the realm.
1534: Cliopatria returns 85 southern Transdanubian cells to Hungary from the Ottoman Empire.
24 February 1538: the Treaty of Nagyvarad divides the kingdom between Ferdinand and John.
24 February 1538: John Zapolya keeps Transylvania and the eastern plain.
1541: with Buda lost, the Habsburg kingdom is governed from Pressburg (Pozsony).
29 August 1541: the Ottomans take Buda and central Hungary becomes Budin Province.
1546: Cliopatria's row ends; royal Hungary passes to the Habsburg Monarchy, central Hungary to the Ottomans, the east to the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom.

wars.name: Stephen I's wars against Gyula, Ajtony and Kean
wars.outcome: Stephen subdues his uncle Gyula and Transylvania; Ajtony is killed by Csanad's army and a bishopric is set up at Csanad; the campaign against Kean is dated c.1003 or the late 1010s.

wars.name: Polish-Hungarian War (1014-1018)
wars.outcome: The Peace of Bautzen (January 1018) 'reportedly required Boleslaw to hand back Morava valley territories'; Steinhubel keeps parts of Slovakia under Polish rule to 1030.

wars.name: Conrad II's invasion of Hungary
wars.outcome: 'Emperor Conrad personally led his armies to Hungary in June 1030', withdrew, and in summer 1031 ceded the lands between the Lajta and Fischa rivers.

wars.name: Conquest of Slavonia and the Croatian succession struggle
wars.outcome: Ladislaus I conquers Slavonia in 1091; Petar Snacic is elected king in 1093 at Knin and Almos is forced back in 1095; Coloman is crowned in Biograd in 1102.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian wars for Dalmatia (1116-1133)
wars.outcome: Venice takes the coastal cities after Coloman's death; Stephen II regains some in 1124, Venice retakes them in 1125, and in 1133 Bela II wins back all but Zadar.

wars.name: Byzantine-Hungarian War (1163-1167)
wars.outcome: Manuel I occupies Syrmia (1164) and Dalmatia (1165) and destroys the Hungarian army at Sirmium on 8 July 1167; the peace 'confirmed Byzantine dominion over central Dalmatia, Bosnia and Syrmia'.

wars.name: Bela III's recovery of Dalmatia and Syrmia
wars.outcome: After Manuel I's death on 24 September 1180 Bela restores his suzerainty in Dalmatia by early 1181 and holds Syrmia by May 1182; in the first half of 1183 he advances as far as Nis and Serdica.

wars.name: Hungarian occupation of Halych (1188-1190)
wars.outcome: Bela III expels Roman Mstislavich and gives Halych to his son Andrew; Vladimir escapes and, with Casimir II of Poland, expels Andrew in early 1189 or 1190.

wars.name: Fourth Crusade at Zadar
wars.outcome: 'the armies of the Fourth Crusade took Zadar in 1202'; Zadar stayed contested between Venice and the Hungarian crown until the Treaty of Zadar of 1358.

wars.name: Bosnian Crusade
wars.outcome: Duke Coloman and Bishop John campaign for five years (1235-1240); Coloman withdraws in 1241 after the Tatar invasion and Ninoslav retakes control.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Hungary
wars.outcome: The Mongols break through the Verecke Pass on 12 March 1241, annihilate Bela IV's army at Mohi on 11 April, cross the frozen Danube in early 1242 and withdraw in March 1242 after Ogodei's death.

wars.name: Bela IV's war with Ottokar II over Styria
wars.outcome: Peace of Pressburg 1 May 1254: Styria to Bela; Ottokar wins at Kressenbrunn on 12 June 1260; Peace of Vienna 31 March 1261: Bela renounces Styria.

wars.name: Charles I's wars against the oligarchs
wars.outcome: After the Arpad line ended on 14 January 1301 'most territories remained out of royal control'; Charles won at Rozgony in 1312, Csak died in 1321 and the Babonic and Subic were subjugated in 1323.

wars.name: Louis I's Neapolitan campaigns
wars.outcome: Louis enters the kingdom on 24 December 1347, leaves in May 1348 because of the Black Death, returns in April 1350 and withdraws all troops in 1351.

wars.name: Hungarian-Venetian War of 1356-1358
wars.outcome: Louis invades Venetian lands in summer 1356, besieges Treviso on 27 July and marches to Dalmatia in July 1357; by the Treaty of Zadar (18 February 1358) Venice renounces Dalmatia.

wars.name: Louis I's war in Bosnia
wars.outcome: Louis invades in spring 1363 and takes Kljuc, but Srebrenik holds; in March 1367 Tvrtko returns and regains Donji Kraji, Rama, Hum and Usora.

wars.name: Louis I's Vidin campaign
wars.outcome: Louis seizes Vidin and imprisons Ivan Stratsimir in May or June 1365 and his troops occupy the realm within three months.

wars.name: Crusade of Nicopolis
wars.outcome: The crusaders 'were routed in the battle of Nicopolis in 1396'; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Venetian takeover of the Dalmatian coast
wars.outcome: Ladislaus of Naples sells his claims to Venice in 1409 and 'the republic forced the settlements on the Dalmatian coasts one by one to accept her suzerainty'.

wars.name: Crusade of Varna
wars.outcome: 'The Ottomans annihilated the Christian forces at the Battle of Varna in 1444, during which Wladyslaw was killed'; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Bohemian-Hungarian War (1468-1478)
wars.outcome: Matthias declares war on George of Podebrady on 31 March 1468, is elected king of Bohemia at Olomouc on 3 May 1469; the Peace of Olomouc ratified on 21 July 1478 gives him Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia and Vladislaus Bohemia proper.

wars.name: Matthias Corvinus's Bosnian campaign
wars.outcome: After Mehmed II's conquest of Bosnia in June 1463 Matthias takes Jajce and the northern forts, organised as the banates of Jajce and Srebrenik.

wars.name: Matthias Corvinus's Ottoman wars
wars.outcome: Matthias captures Sabac on 15 February 1476, helps Moldavia win at the Siret in August 1476 and at Breadfield on 13 October 1479.

wars.name: Austrian-Hungarian War (1477-1488)
wars.outcome: Hungarian victory: the Black Army takes Vienna in 1485 and Wiener Neustadt in 1487; after Matthias's death on 6 April 1490 Frederick III regains the Austrian lands without a serious fight and the Peace of Pressburg (1491) returns Matthias's conquests.

wars.name: Dozsa Rebellion
wars.outcome: The peasant revolt of 9 April - 15 July 1514 (infobox dates) changed no frontier.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Belgrade and the Battle of Mohacs
wars.outcome: Suleiman seizes Belgrade in 1521 and defeats the Hungarian army at Mohacs on 29 August 1526, where Louis II drowns.

wars.name: War of the two kings (Ferdinand and John Zapolya)
wars.outcome: Two kings are elected (Zapolya on 10 November 1526, Ferdinand in December); Ferdinand's army drives John out by 1528; John swears fealty to the sultan on 19 August 1529; the Treaty of Nagyvarad (24 February 1538) divides the kingdom.

wars.name: Ottoman occupation of central Hungary
wars.outcome: Buda is taken by a trick on 29 August 1541 and central Hungary becomes Budin Province; the royal remainder is governed from Pressburg.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate throughout: the Carpathian march, the Danube and Sava lines to Bulgaria and Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia (a union and a vassalage rather than a border), the Halych and Mongol episodes.

The Dalmatian coast is a treaty line from the Treaty of Zadar (18 February 1358) to the Venetian takeover after 1409; the Bohemian line follows the Peace of Olomouc (21 July 1478), the Austrian line the Peace of 1 December 1477 and the…
The 24 February 1538 Treaty of Nagyvarad is a dated division but no survey line; the Ottoman-Habsburg front after 1541 is approximate.
